findings.summary: THE CITED MEASUREMENT IS INVERTED, AND THE CLAIM IT IS OFFERED AS EVIDENCE FOR IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE RECORD SAYS. The new M4.8a clause reads: 'a 2-3 entry golden re-encodes correctly on most runs. That is measured history here, not theory -- M4.1's row records the missing-sort mutation killed about 1 run in 6 at three streams, and 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing only once raised to six.' M4.1's row (docs/internal/product/backlog-done.md:110) records the reciprocal: 'at three streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6. Raised to six streams; measured 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing where the reviewer had measured 1 in 6 passing.' Survived ~1 run in 6 means KILLED ~5 runs in 6. So the record says a three-stream golden caught the missing-sort mutation about 83% of the time; this row says it caught it about 17% of the time, and builds on that inversion the load-bearing sentence 'a 2-3 entry golden re-encodes correctly on most runs', which the record contradicts -- at three streams the mutation re-encoded correctly on a MINORITY of runs. The prescription that follows (six streams, distinct non-default values, values-then-byte-identity) is the right prescription and is what M4.1 itself did, so only the number and the 'most runs' generalisation are wrong -- but they are stated as measurement, in the sentence that says 'measured history here, not theory'.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8a's implementer, or any later task deciding how large a golden fixture must be, reads this row as the measured record and carries forward a figure that is 5x wrong in the direction that makes small goldens look blind: a reader concluding a 2-3 entry golden is ~83% blind to an ordering mutation will either over-build (a rerun-N-fresh-JVMs harness for a fixture that already kills the mutation most runs) or, when someone later checks the citation against backlog-done.md:110 and finds it reversed, distrust both rows -- and neither is reconstructible afterwards, exactly the state review.md rule 12's own '8 versus 7' paragraph records the tree ending up in ('Neither is reconstructible, so the split is recorded rather than settled'). This is the failure non-negotiable 4 names: a number reported as measured that the measurement does not support. It is also the class of defect round 1's F3 was majored for -- a claim the record does not support -- reappearing in the prose the F3/F5 fix added. Remedy is one clause: state it as the record does ('a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6 at three streams -- so a small golden is probabilistic, not blind -- and six streams measured 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing'), which supports the same six-stream prescription without misquoting the measurement.

findings.summary: TWO COPIES OF THE SAME NEW CONSTRAINT, WRITTEN IN THIS DIFF, DISAGREE. The summary row states a prohibition -- 'THE KEY MUST NOT LAND WHERE RECOVERY LISTS' -- while the notes row it points at (docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md:325) leaves two options open and treats them as equally acceptable: 'Either the key goes outside the listed prefix or recovery filters by suffix.' The suffix-filter option lands the key exactly where recovery lists, which the summary forbids. Worse, the notes row still OPENS by mandating that key ('Write a checkpoint every K deltas or T seconds, both configuration, at ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch:016x>/ckpt/<seq:016x>.ckpt'), so within the two files the same key is mandated (notes, leading clause), permitted-with-a-filter (notes, fix clause) and prohibited (backlog.md headline). Mechanism itself is verified correct: CommitLog.logPrefix() is '<prefix>/ctl/log/0/<epoch:016x>/' (sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLog.java:114), ChainReplay.chainEnd lists it undelimited and reads the last key (ChainReplay.java:94-116), applyChain hands every listed key to read() with no suffix filter (ChainReplay.java:308-320), and 'ckpt/' sorts after every 16-hex-digit delta key.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md is the file every session loads whole (that is what check-session-load.sh bounds), so the prohibition is the copy most readers see, and it silently removes an option the notes call legitimate. A session that picks M4.8b from backlog.md and follows its headline moves the key out of ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch>/ entirely; a session that reads the notes first may implement the suffix filter and then find the summary row saying its choice was forbidden. Neither produces a broken tree, so nothing catches the disagreement -- it is discovered by the next reader, who now has to decide which of two same-commit statements binds. This is the one-copy-versus-duplicate failure the M4.8 source row itself shouts about two sections earlier, reintroduced by the fix for it.

findings.summary: THE TWO FIXES ARE OFFERED AS INTERCHANGEABLE AND ARE NOT, ON THE PROJECT'S OWN AXIS. (a) 'recovery filters by suffix' keeps checkpoints under logPrefix(), so ChainReplay.chainEnd and applyChain keep LISTing a prefix whose key count grows with checkpoints -- nothing deletes them before M7 -- and each 1,000-key page is one LIST, so recovery's LIST count grows with UPTIME even after the decode failure is fixed. The row is careful about the GET consequence of the unfixed case and silent about the LIST consequence of its own fix, and the takeover test it mandates ('asserted by a takeover test with checkpoints present') is specified for correctness only, with no request-count dimension -- while the M4.8c row two sections down correctly insists the discriminator is total requests constant in checkpoint count. SPEC.md:279-284 is where this bites: recovery is tier 3 of M5's fallback ladder run by up to 300 plugin nodes against cost.md R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling. (b) 'the key goes outside the listed prefix' contradicts SPEC.md:269, which states the grammar ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch:016x>/ckpt/<seq:016x>.ckpt normatively, and neither row says that choosing it makes the SPEC wrong and requires amending it in the same commit (sdd.md rule 8: a spec that turns out to be wrong is amended, not worked around). The M4.6 precedent shows the SPEC's TASK TABLE is deliberately not updated for a split, so that copy is fine -- but SPEC section 'Checkpoint key grammar' is a design statement, not a task row.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8b's implementer picks the suffix filter because the row presents it as equivalent and cheaper, writes the takeover test the row asks for, and lands green -- with recovery's LIST count now a function of uptime on the exact path SPEC.md:279-284 says breaches R15's ceiling at M5 fan-out rather than at M4's scale. Nothing catches it: no cost meter exists (cost.md 'Enforcement'), M4.9's zero-LIST criterion is a different task, and the mandated takeover test asserts decode succeeds, not what it cost. Alternatively the implementer moves the key, and SPEC.md:269 is left stating a grammar nothing in the tree writes, with the next reader of the SPEC building M4.8c and M4.9 against a ckpt/ prefix that does not exist.

findings.summary: THE ROW ASSERTS A PROPERTY THE FIX REMOVED FROM IT. It reads 'this row is the source text and is not itself implemented. The source text is preserved in the sub-rows' -- but the source text was deleted from this row in this diff, so the sentence claiming to BE the source text is now the only thing left of it. The sibling precedent in the same file, four sections earlier, does it the other way: backlog-notes.md:161 (M4.6) carries the split banner AND retains the full source text under it. I checked every clause of the deleted M4.8 text against the three sub-rows and none was lost (record fields to M4.8a, K/T plus key grammar plus the ADR-0022 ordering argument to M4.8b, zero-LIST discovery plus candidates plus the >5,000 workload to M4.8c, the not-the-offset-index rationale and the ~38 KiB figure to M4.8a) -- so nothing is missing today.
findings.failure_scenario: The notes row exists so a split can be audited later against what the milestone originally asked for. With the text gone, the only surviving copy of the pre-split wording is git history, and the row asserting it is the source text tells a future auditor to stop looking. A subsequent re-split or re-scoping of M4.8a-c then has nothing in the tree to check its clause coverage against -- the check I was able to run this round is not repeatable next round -- while M4.6's row two screens up still supports exactly that check.
